## Summary

I completed the search and submitted a specification:

**Final specification:** F28 (long) + F36 (long) + F03 (long), equal-weighted
**In-sample Sharpe:** 1.0866 (net of costs)

**Process:**
1. Declared three stopping rules upfront: stop if best-so-far Sharpe exceeds 1.2, stop after 4 failures, or stop if the last gain is ≤0.02.
2. Skipped `pick_prior` since I had no data-independent reason to favor any specific feature — the feature summary only described statistical properties (kurtosis, autocorrelation, turnover), not predictive power.
3. Used `init` to anchor on the best single feature (F28, Sharpe 0.8545).
4. Used `extend_best` twice, adding F36 (→0.9876) then F03 (→1.0866), reaching the 3-feature cap.
5. Called `refine` to check signs — no change, confirming signs were already optimal.
6. My `last_gain_at_most(0.02)` rule fired after the no-op refine, correctly signaling diminishing returns, so I stopped rather than continuing to search (which would have made the run non-replayable).

**Prediction:** I forecast an out-of-sample Sharpe of **0.60 (SD 0.35)**, applying a substantial discount (~45%) to the in-sample 1.09 figure to account for typical in-sample-to-out-of-sample degradation, even though the search itself was short and disciplined (only 3 greedy steps across 40 low-correlation features).
